cards.summary: [Default] entry of the Additive for Blob Brush library: merged onto an object it keeps the object's own fill and adds only a thin dark grey hairline outline (a thin stroke) around every shape; no other effect. (Thumbnail: the style merged by script with mergeTo onto a plain blue star and 'PGD' outlines, as Alt-click adds it; not a shipped preview.)
use_for: quick thin dark keyline around a filled shape or outlined type
avoid: expecting it to leave the object unchanged: the merge adds a thin dark hairline stroke
applying it with a plain click: that resets the object to Illustrator's default white fill and black stroke
cards.applies_to: any page item (path, compound path, group, outlined type); an additive graphic style made to be added on top of the object's existing appearance (Alt-click / mergeTo), so the object keeps its own fill and stroke. The style must exist in the target document.
cards.how_to_apply: Panel: Window > Graphic Style Libraries > Additive for Blob Brush, select the object, Alt-click '[Default]' to add it to the current appearance (a plain click replaces the appearance). Script: app.open("C:/Program Files/Adobe/Adobe Illustrator 2026/Presets/en_US/Graphic Styles/Additive for Blob Brush.ai"), then on an item in that document doc.graphicStyles.getByName("[Default]").mergeTo(pageItem) to add it (as rendered) or .applyTo(pageItem) (the harvested call) to replace the appearance; item.duplicate(target.layers[0], ElementPlacement.PLACEATEND) carries the style into the target document; close the library with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES.

verified.note: Blue star and PGD keep their fill but gain a thin dark grey hairline outline that the other additive renders lack.

review.changes: summary, look, use_for, avoid rewritten: the merge adds a thin dark hairline outline, it is not a no-op; confidence high -> medium
